modules.title: Measurement Standards, Precision & Comprehensive Vector Analysis
modules.rationale: Establishes standard scientific measurement units, uncertainty, and vector mathematics, providing the mathematical tools required for all subsequent mechanics modules.

sequence.text: SI base units (m, kg, s, K, A, mol, cd) and prefix orders (10^(12) to 10^(-12)).
Derived units, dimensional analysis, scientific notation, and significant figures.
Scalar vs. vector quantities; Graphical vector addition (triangle, parallelogram, polygon laws).
2D analytical vector resolution into rectangular components (A_x = Acosθ, A_y = Asinθ).
Unit vectors (hat{i}, hat{j}, hat{k}) and vector addition via components.
Scalar (dot) product (vec{A}·vec{B} = ABcosθ) and vector (cross) product (vec{A}×vec{B}).

prerequisites: High school algebra and basic trigonometry (sin, cos, tan)
modules.masteryCheckpoint: Given vec{A} = 3hat{i} - 4hat{j} and vec{B} = -2hat{i} + 5hat{j}, calculate the magnitude of the resultant vec{R} = 2vec{A} - vec{B}, find the unit vector pointing in the direction of vec{A}, and calculate the angle between vec{A} and vec{B} using the dot product.

modules.title: Unified Kinematics in One and Two Dimensions
modules.rationale: Merges 1D linear motion with 2D projectile trajectories and rotational kinematics, showing how multi-dimensional paths can be decomposed into simpler 1D components.

references.unitTitle: Motion in One and Two Dimensions

sequence.text: Position, displacement, average/instantaneous speed, and velocity.
Graphical analysis of motion: slope of s-t gives velocity, slope of v-t gives acceleration, area under v-t gives displacement.
The five kinematic equations for constant acceleration in 1D.
Vertical free fall under gravity (a = -g) and 1D relative velocity (v_AB = v_A ± v_B).
2D projectile motion: independent horizontal velocity (a_x = 0) and vertical acceleration (a_y = -g).
Derivation of projectile time of flight (T = (2usinθ)/(g)), maximum height (H = (u^2sin^2θ)/(2g)), and range (R = (u^2sin 2θ)/(g)).
Uniform circular motion: angular velocity (omega), tangential velocity (v_t = omega r), and centripetal acceleration (a_c = (v^2)/(r) = omega^2 r).
Rotational kinematics equations with constant angular acceleration (θ, omega, α).

modules.masteryCheckpoint: A football is kicked at 20\,m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Calculate its total time of flight, its maximum elevation, its horizontal range, and its velocity vector at t = 1.5\,s.

modules.title: Complete Dynamics, Work-Energy & Momentum Systems
modules.rationale: Unifies the causes of translational and rotational motion with the fundamental conservation laws of physical mechanics (Mechanical Energy and Linear/Angular Momentum).

sequence.text: Newton's Three Laws of Motion, inertia, mass vs. weight (W = mg).
Static and kinetic friction: F_s ≤ μ_s F_N and F_k = μ_k F_N; inclined plane dynamics and critical angle of repose (θ_c = tan^(-1)μ_s).
Free-body diagrams, connected bodies over pulleys, and apparent weight in accelerating elevators (T = m(g ± a)).
Work done by constant and varying forces (W = int F\,dx); spring elasticity (Hooke's Law: F = -kx, PE = (1)/(2)kx^2).
Work-Energy Theorem (W_net = Δ KE) and conservation of mechanical energy (KE_i + PE_i = KE_f + PE_f + W_friction).
Power: average and instantaneous rate of work (P = (W)/(t) = vec{F}·vec{v}).
Impulse-Momentum Theorem (vec{J} = vec{F}_netΔ t = Δvec{P}) and isolated momentum conservation (Σvec{P}_i = Σvec{P}_f).
Collisions in 1D: elastic (e = 1), inelastic, and perfectly inelastic (v_f = (m_1 u_1 + m_2 u_2)/(m_1 + m_2)); ballistic pendulum.
Center of mass calculation and variable mass systems (rocket propulsion: F_thrust = v_rel(Δ m)/(Δ t)).
Rotational dynamics: torque (tau = r Fsinθ = Iα), moment of inertia (I = Σ m_i r_i^2), rotational kinetic energy, and angular momentum conservation (L = Iomega).
Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation (F_g = G(m_1 m_2)/(r^2)), orbital speeds, and Kepler's three laws of planetary motion.

modules.masteryCheckpoint: A 2\,kg block released from rest at the top of a 5\,m high, 30° incline slides down with coefficient of kinetic friction μ_k = 0.2. Use the Work-Energy Theorem to find its velocity at the bottom. Then, calculate the rebound height if it collides elastically with a stationary 3\,kg block.

modules.title: Statics, Solid Elasticity, Simple Machines & Fluid Mechanics
modules.rationale: Examines static equilibrium across mechanical systems, solid materials under load, simple machines, and pressurized fluids.

references.unitTitle: Elasticity and Static Equilibrium of Rigid Bodies

sequence.text: First and Second conditions of static equilibrium (Σvec{F} = 0, Σvec{tau} = 0).
Elasticity, plasticity, tensile stress (σ = (F)/(A)), tensile strain (epsilon = (Δ L)/(L_0)), Young's Modulus (Y = (σ)/(epsilon)), and elastic limits.
Metrics of simple machines: AMA = (Load)/(Effort), VR = (d_E)/(d_L), eta = (AMA)/(VR)× 100\%.
Principles of levers (classes 1, 2, 3), inclined planes, wedges, screws, wheel and axle, and pulley systems (VR = n).
Fluid statics: density, specific gravity, pressure definition, atmospheric pressure, and gauge vs. absolute pressure (P_abs = P_atm + rho gh).
Pascal's Principle and hydraulic lift calculations ((F_1)/(A_1) = (F_2)/(A_2)).
Archimedes' Principle: buoyant force (F_B = rho_fluidV_dispg) and the law of flotation.
Fluid dynamics: Equation of Continuity (A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2) for steady laminar flow.

modules.masteryCheckpoint: A uniform 10\,m ladder of mass 20\,kg leans against a smooth vertical wall at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. Calculate the minimum coefficient of static friction between the ladder and the ground needed to prevent slipping. Then, find the apparent weight of a 500\,cm^3 iron block submerged in water.

modules.title: Oscillations, Mechanical Waves, Sound & Geometrical Optics
modules.rationale: Unifies wave motion across mechanical oscillations, acoustic compression waves, electromagnetic radiation, and ray optics.

references.unitTitle: Application of Physics in Other Fields

sequence.text: Periodic oscillation parameters: period (T), frequency (f = (1)/(T)), amplitude (A), wavelength (λ), and speed (v = fλ).
Simple Harmonic Motion: simple pendulum (T = 2πsqrt{(L)/(g)}) and mass-spring systems (T = 2πsqrt{(m)/(k)}).
Transverse vs. longitudinal waves; sound waves, speed of sound in media, and temperature variations (v ≈ 331 + 0.6\,T).
Wave phenomena: reflection (echoes), refraction in atmospheric temperature gradients, diffraction, and interference.
The Electromagnetic Spectrum: radio to gamma rays in order of frequency and energy (E = hf).
Laws of reflection and refraction; Snell's Law (n_1sinθ_1 = n_2sinθ_2); total internal reflection and critical angle (sinθ_c = (n_2)/(n_1)).
Image formation in plane mirrors, spherical mirrors (concave/convex), and thin lenses (converging/diverging).
The Mirror and Thin Lens equations ((1)/(f) = (1)/(u) + (1)/(v)) and magnification (m = -(v)/(u) or (v)/(u)).
Optical instruments (microscopes, telescopes) and human eye defect corrections (myopia and hypermetropia).
Color addition of light (Red, Green, Blue) and subtractive filters.

prerequisites: Module 1 (geometry and trigonometry) and Module 2 (kinematic variables)
modules.masteryCheckpoint: An object is placed 15\,cm in front of a concave mirror with a focal length of 10\,cm. Calculate the image distance, magnification, and state whether the image is real or virtual. Next, determine the critical angle for light passing from water (n = 1.33) into air (n = 1.00).

modules.title: Thermal Physics, Calorimetry & Phase Transitions
modules.rationale: Unifies microscopic molecular kinetic theory with macroscopic temperature scales, thermal expansion, heat transfer mechanisms, and phase change calorimetry.

sequence.text: Concept of temperature as average molecular kinetic energy; Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics and thermal equilibrium.
Thermometric properties, fixed points, and scale conversions between Celsius, Kelvin, and Fahrenheit.
Thermal expansion in solids: linear (Δ L = α L_0Δ T), superficial (Δ A = 2α A_0Δ T), and cubical/volume (Δ V = 3α V_0Δ T); apparent liquid expansion.
Heat as energy in transit; mechanisms of heat transfer: Conduction (H = kA(Δ T)/(L)), Convection, and Radiation (Stefan-Boltzmann).
Specific heat capacity (Q = mcΔ T) and molar heat capacity.
Latent heat of fusion (L_f) and vaporization (L_v); heating/cooling curves and phase change thermodynamics.
Phase diagrams: equilibrium lines, triple point, and critical point.
Quantitative calorimetry: heat lost by hot bodies equals heat gained by cold bodies (Q_lost = Q_gained).

prerequisites: Module 1 (measurement units) and Module 3 (work and conservation of energy)
modules.masteryCheckpoint: A 0.5\,kg block of aluminum at 100°C is dropped into an insulated calorimeter containing 1.0\,kg of water and a 0.2\,kg copper stirrer at 20°C. Calculate the final equilibrium temperature of the mixture given the specific heat capacities of aluminum, copper, and water.

modules.title: Electrostatics, Electric Fields & Capacitance
modules.rationale: Develops electrostatic theory from point charges and Coulomb forces to electric fields, potentials, and energy storage in capacitors.

sequence.text: Properties of electric charges, law of conservation of charge, and charge quantization (q = ne).
Methods of charging: friction, conduction, and induction; electroscopes and lightning.
Coulomb's Law for point charges: F = k(|q_1 q_2|)/(r^2) and vector superposition for multiple charges.
Electric field strength vec{E} = frac{vec{F}}{q_0} = k(q)/(r^2)hat{r}; electric field lines and electric flux (Phi_E = vec{E}·vec{A}).
Electric potential energy (U = k(q Q)/(r)) and electric potential (V = (U)/(q) = k(Q)/(r)).
Relation between uniform electric field and potential difference: E = -(Δ V)/(d); equipotential surfaces.
Capacitance fundamentals (C = (Q)/(V)); parallel-plate capacitance (C = (kappaepsilon_0 A)/(d)) and dielectric constant (kappa).
Capacitor combinations: Series (frac{1}{C_eq} = Σ(1)/(C_i)) and Parallel (C_eq = Σ C_i); energy stored in capacitors (U = (1)/(2)CV^2).

prerequisites: Module 1 (vector components) and Module 3 (work and potential energy)
modules.masteryCheckpoint: Point charges q_1 = +4\,μ C and q_2 = -2\,μ C are separated by 10\,cm. Find the net electric field at the midpoint between them. Then, calculate the equivalent capacitance and total energy stored when three 6\,μ F capacitors are connected in series across a 12\,V battery.

modules.title: Direct Current Electricity, Circuit Networks & Measuring Devices
modules.rationale: Unifies electric current, resistance, network analysis, precision electrical measurements, and domestic electrical safety.

sequence.text: Electric current definition (I = (Δ q)/(Δ t)); microscopic drift velocity (I = n q v_d A) and current density (J = (I)/(A) = σ E).
Ohm's Law (V = IR), electrical resistance, and resistivity (R = rho(L)/(A)).
Series and parallel resistor combinations and equivalent resistance.
Electromotive force (EMF) and terminal potential difference: V_terminal = mathcal{E} - Ir.
Kirchhoff's Circuit Rules: Junction Rule (Σ I_in = Σ I_out) and Loop Rule (Σ mathcal{E} - Σ IR = 0).
Precision measuring circuits: Wheatstone Bridge for unknown resistance ((R_1)/(R_2) = (R_3)/(R_x)) and the Potentiometer.
Conversion of a galvanometer into an ammeter (using parallel shunt R_s) and a voltmeter (using series multiplier R_m).
Electric power dissipation (P = VI = I^2 R = (V^2)/(R)), domestic 220V installation in Ethiopia, grounding, and fuses.

modules.masteryCheckpoint: Use Kirchhoff's rules to calculate the branch currents in a two-loop circuit powered by two opposing EMF sources (12\,V and 6\,V) with internal resistances. Then, calculate the shunt resistance needed to convert a 50\,Ω galvanometer with a 1\,mA full-scale deflection into a 5\,A ammeter.

modules.title: Magnetism, Electromagnetism & Electromagnetic Induction
modules.rationale: Traces the relationship between electricity and magnetism, from magnetic forces on moving charges to magnetic flux and electromagnetic induction in transformers.

sequence.text: Magnetic poles, magnetic dipole properties, and field line mapping.
Earth's magnetic field and navigation compasses.
Magnetic field generated by current-carrying conductors (Biot-Savart and Ampère principles).
Magnetic force on moving charged particles: vec{F}_B = q(vec{v}×vec{B}) → F = q v Bsinθ and circular particle trajectories.
Magnetic force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field: F = I l Bsinθ.
Mutual force between parallel current-carrying conductors: currents in same direction attract; currents in opposite directions repel.
Magnetic flux: Phi_B = vec{B}·vec{A} = B Acosθ (Wb = T· m^2).
Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction: mathcal{E} = -N(ΔPhi_B)/(Δ t).
Lenz's Law: direction of induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux (conservation of energy).
Electric transformers: mutual induction, step-up vs. step-down, and turns ratio ((V_s)/(V_p) = (N_s)/(N_p) = (I_p)/(I_s)).

prerequisites: Module 1 (cross products) and Module 8 (currents and voltages)
modules.masteryCheckpoint: An electron enters a uniform 0.4\,T magnetic field at 5.0× 10^6\,m/s perpendicular to the field lines. Calculate the magnetic force acting on the electron and the radius of its circular path. Next, calculate the average EMF induced in a 500-turn coil of area 0.02\,m^2 when the perpendicular magnetic field drops from 0.8\,T to zero in 0.05\,s.

modules.title: Modern Physics, Nuclear Reactions & Semiconductor Electronics
modules.rationale: Covers 20th-century physics: subatomic nuclear structure, radioactive decay, nuclear energy, and solid-state semiconductor electronics.

sequence.text: Nuclear composition: protons, neutrons, isotopes, and nuclear radius (R = R_0 A^(1/3)).
Mass defect (Δ m) and nuclear binding energy: BE = Δ m· c^2 = Δ m(amu)× 931.5\,MeV; binding energy per nucleon curve.
Natural radioactivity: alpha (α), beta (β^- and β^+), and gamma (γ) decay processes and balancing nuclear equations.
Radioactive decay law: N(t) = N_0 e^(-λ t); decay constant (λ) and half-life relationship (T_1/2 = (ln 2)/(λ)).
Nuclear applications: radiocarbon dating, nuclear medicine, radiotherapy (e.g., Black Lion Hospital), and radiation safety.
Nuclear fission vs. nuclear fusion reactions and chain reactions.
Energy band theory: conductors, insulators, and intrinsic vs. extrinsic semiconductors (P-type and N-type doping).
P-N junction diode: depletion region, forward/reverse bias, and half-wave/full-wave rectification circuits.
Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJT): operating characteristics, emitter-base-collector currents (I_E = I_B + I_C), and switching/amplification.
Digital logic gates: truth tables, Boolean operations (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR), and combinational logic circuits.

modules.masteryCheckpoint: Calculate the binding energy per nucleon of Helium-4 ({}_2^4He) given the masses of a proton, neutron, and alpha particle. If a radioactive sample has a half-life of 8 days, calculate the fraction remaining after 32 days. Finally, draw the truth table for a 2-input NAND gate and show how it can be wired to function as an inverter (NOT gate).
